**I can't give an evidence-backed answer to this question, and the evidence I found doesn't settle it.** The one source that frames the question the same way is a paywalled analyst note. It says the 2030 market size ($2.4bn–$4.1bn) depends almost entirely on whether evaluation consolidates into observability suites or stays standalone. Its abstract doesn't say which outcome it expects. I found no primary evidence on incumbent moves, such as Datadog or other observability vendors shipping evals, M&A, or OpenTelemetry standardisation. Any confident prediction would be my own opinion, not a sourced finding.

## Key Findings
- **The consolidation question is the main uncertainty in the market forecast.** Northgate Analytics estimates the agent evaluation and observability tooling market at about $310M in 2025. It models a 2030 range of $2.4bn–$4.1bn, with the spread driven "almost entirely" by this question. The segment breakdown and vendor shares are paywalled, so I couldn't see its base case. (https://northgate-analytics.example/notes/agent-eval-market-sizing, 2026-07-15) `[single source, abstract only]`
- **Adoption is early, so the category is still forming.** Two surveys put the share of teams running no automated agent evaluation at 62% (AIQ, 1,204 teams, Jan–Feb 2026) and 48% (TechWire, 890 organisations with over 200 employees, June 2026).
  - The gap is mostly sample differences. AIQ's sample was self-selected and spanned all team sizes. TechWire's was larger companies only. (https://aiqreport.com/2026/state-of-agent-evals, https://techwire.example/research/agent-eval-adoption-2026)
  - Both agree adoption is rising and trajectory-level scoring is rare, at 9% in AIQ and 13% in TechWire.
- **Evaluation quality is a gap that observability alone doesn't fill.** AIQ found only 11% of LLM-as-judge users had calibrated their judge against human labels. The median golden set was 22 tasks, which the report calls too small to be useful. (https://aiqreport.com/2026/state-of-agent-evals) This suggests eval is a methodology problem and not only a telemetry problem. That is a plausible argument for standalone vendors, but the report doesn't draw that conclusion. The inference is mine.
- **At least one standalone vendor positions itself as complementary to observability.** EvalTools (Berlin, 31 employees) says it is "not an observability vendor" and integrates with OpenTelemetry instead of replacing it. It sells golden datasets, trajectory scoring, calibrated judges, and CI gates. (https://evaltools.io/about, 2026-04-02) This is a vendor's own positioning, so it shows intent and not market outcome.

## Detailed Analysis

**What the evidence supports**

| Question | Status |
|---|---|
| Is the market growing? | Directionally yes (Northgate forecast, rising adoption in two surveys) |
| Are incumbent observability vendors absorbing evals? | **Not established.** No source retrieved |
| Have any standalone eval vendors been acquired? | **Not established.** Search returned nothing |
| Is there a standards layer (OpenTelemetry) that could commoditise tracing? | **Not established.** Only EvalTools' own mention |
| Which outcome does the analyst base case favour? | Unknown (paywalled) |

**Sources I excluded**
- "The 17 Best Agent Evaluation Platforms in 2026" (top-ai-tools-daily.example) discloses AI-assisted generation and affiliate links, and its sources are vague. It claims "91% of agents fail in production" and that EvalTools has about $40M ARR and 12,000 enterprise customers. I did not use these figures. The ARR and customer count also conflict with EvalTools' own 31-employee profile, though I can't rule either out. `[UNVERIFIED]`

**My reasoning, not sourced findings**
- Consolidation pressure would come from tracing and data collection becoming commodity infrastructure, with incumbents bundling evals. The counter-pressure is that evaluation depends on datasets, judge calibration, and CI workflow, which differ from monitoring. Whether the second force survives to 2030 is what the Northgate spread appears to encode.
- A split outcome seems plausible: tracing goes to the suites, and rigorous pre-release eval stays specialised or becomes a feature of agent frameworks. I haven't verified this.

## Recommendations
1. **Don't treat "consolidates by 2030" as established in any deliverable.** If you need a position, label it as judgement and cite the Northgate abstract for the uncertainty only.
2. **To close the gap, collect three things:**
   - incumbents' current agent-eval features, from their own docs and changelogs;
   - 2024–2026 M&A and funding for eval vendors;
   - the Northgate full note, if the subscription is worth it.
   I couldn't reach these with the current search index. Direct vendor-site fetches or a Firecrawl crawl would likely do better.
3. **Cheap leading indicators to watch:** whether eval vendors keep emphasising OpenTelemetry interop, whether suites add calibrated judges and CI gates, and whether surveys start asking which tool category teams use for evals.
4. **Relevance to the owner:** this has no direct tie to the Atelier Alfa or Acme Training offers. It could matter for AI/QA teaching content, because eval methodology (golden sets, judge calibration) is where the surveys show the biggest gaps.

| Dimension | AIQ Report | TechWire |
|---|---|---|
| Published | 2026-03-12 | 2026-06-02 |
